quick.summary: Why users click buttons repeatedly, and the simple fix to stop it.
quick.takeaway: Always give immediate visual feedback when a user takes an action.

beats.line: People keep clicking pay three times. Why do they do that?
Picture an elevator. You press the button to call it.
And the little ring lights up so I know it worked.
Right. If the light is broken, what do you do?
I mash the button five times because I think it is broken.
Users do the same. The app lacks visibility of system status.
Can I just say we are giving no feedback?
Much better. No feedback causes panic.
The app needs to show it is working on their request.
I will add a loading spinner when they click pay.
Exactly. Show them you heard them.

quiz.question: Why do users repeatedly click a submit button?
options: They want to break the app
quiz.explanation: When an app fails to show it is processing a request, users assume the click failed.

quiz.question: Providing visual feedback prevents panic clicks.
quiz.explanation: Even a simple loading spinner reassures the user that the system is responding.
